front: An amplitude-modulated (AM) waveform has an envelope that varies between a maximum of \(V_{\max}=12\ \text{V}\) and a minimum of \(V_{\min}=4\ \text{V}\). Determine the modulation index \(m\).
explanation: For AM the envelope peaks are \(V_{\max}=A_c(1+m)\) and \(V_{\min}=A_c(1-m)\). Solving for \(m\): \[m=\frac{V_{\max}-V_{\min}}{V_{\max}+V_{\min}}=\frac{12-4}{12+4}=\frac{8}{16}=0.5.\] The carrier is 50% modulated.

front: An AM transmitter radiates a carrier power of \(P_c=500\ \text{W}\) and is modulated by a single tone to a depth of \(m=0.6\). Find the total power contained in the two sidebands.
explanation: Total transmitted power is \(P_t=P_c\left(1+\tfrac{m^2}{2}\right)\), so the sideband power is the excess over the carrier: \[P_{sb}=P_c\cdot\frac{m^2}{2}=500\cdot\frac{0.6^2}{2}=500\cdot0.18=90\ \text{W}.\] The upper and lower sidebands share this equally, 45 W each.

front: A frequency-modulated (FM) signal has a peak frequency deviation of \(\Delta f=75\ \text{kHz}\) when the modulating tone frequency is \(f_m=15\ \text{kHz}\). Determine the modulation index \(\beta\).
explanation: The FM modulation index is the ratio of peak frequency deviation to modulating frequency: \[\beta=\frac{\Delta f}{f_m}=\frac{75\ \text{kHz}}{15\ \text{kHz}}=5.\]

front: An FM signal has a peak frequency deviation of \(\Delta f=30\ \text{kHz}\) and a highest modulating frequency of \(f_m=5\ \text{kHz}\). Estimate the transmission bandwidth using Carson's rule.
explanation: Carson's rule estimates the FM bandwidth as \[B=2(\Delta f+f_m)=2(30\ \text{kHz}+5\ \text{kHz})=2(35\ \text{kHz})=70\ \text{kHz}.\]

front: An angle-modulated signal is \(v(t)=10\cos\!\left[2\pi(10^{8})t+6\sin\!\left(2\pi(10^{3})t\right)\right]\ \text{V}\). Treating it as an FM signal, find the peak frequency deviation \(\Delta f\).
explanation: The phase term is \(\beta\sin(2\pi f_m t)\) with modulation index \(\beta=6\) and modulating frequency \(f_m=10^{3}\ \text{Hz}\). For FM \(\beta=\Delta f/f_m\), so \[\Delta f=\beta f_m=6\times1000\ \text{Hz}=6\ \text{kHz}.\]

front: An analog voice signal band-limited to \(4\ \text{kHz}\) is sampled at the Nyquist rate, and each sample is encoded with \(8\) bits. Determine the PCM bit rate.
explanation: The Nyquist sampling rate is \(f_s=2\times4\ \text{kHz}=8000\ \text{samples/s}\). With \(8\) bits per sample, \[R=f_s\times n=8000\times8=64{,}000\ \text{bps}=64\ \text{kbps}.\]

front: A PCM system uses \(L=64\) uniform quantization levels. How many bits are required to encode each sample?
explanation: The number of bits \(n\) must satisfy \(2^{n}\ge L\). For \(L=64\): \[n=\log_2 64=6\ \text{bits}\quad(2^6=64).\]

front: For a uniform \(n\)-bit PCM quantizer, the signal-to-quantization-noise ratio is approximately \(\text{SNR}\approx(6.02n+1.76)\ \text{dB}\). Estimate the SNR of a \(10\)-bit quantizer.
An amplifier raises a signal's power from \(2\ \text{mW}\) to \(200\ \text{mW}\). Express the power gain in decibels.
A receiver detects an input signal power of \(1\ \mu\text{W}\). Express this power level in dBm.
A communication receiver has a signal power of \(50\ \text{mW}\) and a noise power of \(50\ \mu\text{W}\). Express the signal-to-noise ratio in decibels.
explanation: First form the linear ratio: \(\text{SNR}=\dfrac{50\ \text{mW}}{0.05\ \text{mW}}=1000\). Then \[\text{SNR}_{\text{dB}}=10\log_{10}(1000)=10(3)=30\ \text{dB}.\]

front: A modem transmits at a symbol (baud) rate of \(2400\ \text{symbols/s}\) using \(16\)-QAM. Determine the resulting bit rate.
explanation: Each \(16\)-QAM symbol carries \(\log_2 16=4\) bits. Therefore \[R_b=R_s\times\log_2 M=2400\times4=9600\ \text{bps}.\]

front: A QPSK link carries a bit rate of \(2\ \text{Mbps}\). Determine the channel symbol (baud) rate.
explanation: QPSK maps \(\log_2 4=2\) bits onto each symbol, so the symbol rate is \[R_s=\frac{R_b}{\log_2 M}=\frac{2\times10^{6}}{2}=1\times10^{6}\ \text{symbols/s}=1\ \text{Mbaud}.\]

front: A noiseless channel of bandwidth \(B=3\ \text{kHz}\) transmits using \(M=4\) discrete signal levels. Using the Nyquist relation, find the maximum data rate.
explanation: The Nyquist capacity of a noiseless channel is \[C=2B\log_2 M=2(3000)\log_2 4=2(3000)(2)=12{,}000\ \text{bps}=12\ \text{kbps}.\]

front: A channel has a bandwidth of \(B=3\ \text{kHz}\) and a signal-to-noise power ratio of \(7\). Find the Shannon channel capacity.
A discrete source emits one of \(8\) equally likely symbols. How much information (in bits) does each symbol convey?
explanation: For an equally likely symbol with probability \(p=1/8\), the self-information is \[I=\log_2\frac{1}{p}=\log_2 8=3\ \text{bits}.\]

front: A source emits four symbols with probabilities \(\{\tfrac12,\tfrac14,\tfrac18,\tfrac18\}\). Compute the source entropy \(H\).
A \((7,4)\) Hamming code maps \(4\) data bits into a \(7\)-bit codeword. Determine the code rate.
explanation: Code rate is the ratio of information bits to total transmitted bits: \[R=\frac{k}{n}=\frac{4}{7}\approx0.571.\] The remaining \(3\) bits are parity checks.
